title: Mendor's Library
prerequisites: A way through the locked door: a magic-user with Knock memorized, or a hired THEURGIST.
Mirrors bought at the New Phlan general store and equipped before the Rhetoric stacks.
Commission #3 may be heard from the clerk first; rewards are paid even if it was not offered.
XP figures assume exactly six characters.

scenarios.title: Open the locked door E3 with Knock
steps: From Kuto's Well walk to the library door (exit E3). It is locked.
Have a thief try to pick it: it fails every time.
Have a Strength 18/00 character bash it: it may fail.
Cast Knock: the door opens.
Step through; the party is in Mendor's Library (ECL 15).
expect: Knock always opens the door.
A thief never opens it.
Bashing can succeed but is unreliable.
branches: Hire a THEURGIST (#110, L4 magic-user) at New Phlan hall 14 for Knock; see theurgist-dismissal-lock-in.
Enter instead by E1 or E2; the digest does not say whether those are locked.
sources: Clue Book p.11-12 storyline ('He had the library magically sealed')
disagreements: Lock: [P] v2.00 'a thief can never pick them; Knock always works'; [GB] thieves 'have to be higher than level 4'; [SP] 'opened with bashing, picking, or knock'; Clue Book 'wizard-locked doors' and Dispel Magic removes locking spells, which [P] does not say (digest §7 item 11).
Exits: [P] lists three (E1 Kuto's Well, E2 Textile House, E3 the locked door); Clue Book p.12 says 'leave through one of the two doors'.
scenarios.notes: The digest's wording is inconsistent: 'Getting in: E3 is a locked door ... Other exits: E1 -> Kuto's Well; E2 -> Textile House', while §3.3 says Kuto's Well E3 leads to the library. Which library exit is the locked one, and its coordinates, must be read from the map data. The digest does not quantify the bash chance. Game text block 15 has no line for the locked door; the prompt is generated by the engine. Barred-door state is not saved ([P] §4 UI and files).

scenarios.title: Dismissing the Knock caster inside can lock the party in
steps: Enter with a hired THEURGIST as the only Knock caster.
Inside the library, dismiss the THEURGIST.
Try to leave by the locked door.
expect: With no Knock available and the door locked again, the party cannot open it ([P]: 'possible to lock yourself inside').
scenarios.notes: The digest does not say when the door re-locks or whether the other exits offer a way out, so a test can only assert that the locked door again needs Knock. Treat as a warning to test authors as much as a scenario.

scenarios.title: Cross the garden and meet the green slime
steps: Enter the garden (location 1). The game prints 'YOU SEE WHAT ONCE WAS A GARDEN, NOW-WEED FILLED. THE PLEASANT POND HAS BECOME A SWAMP.'
Each move in the garden rolls a 7 in 26 chance of slime, resolved by a surprise roll (the slime's roll is at -2 when the party is in search mode).
Avoided: 'AS YOU MOVE THROUGH THE GARDEN YOU SEE A STRANGE GREEN PLANT GROWTH WHICH YOU RECOGNIZE AS GREEN SLIME. YOU CAREFULLY MOVE AROUND IT.'
Not avoided: 'YOU STEP INTO A STRANGE GREEN PLANT GROWTH... IT'S GREEN SLIME! QUICKLY, YOU SCRAPE IT OFF, TAKING A GOOD DEAL OF DAMAGE.' A random character takes 1d4 damage.
After 7 slime encounters the game prints 'YOU NOW CAREFULLY AVOID THE GREEN SLIME.'
expect: Slime chance 7 in 26 per move.
A failed avoidance costs one random character 1d4 hit points.
After 7 encounters avoidance is automatic and no further damage occurs.
sources: Clue Book p.11-12 location 9 'Beware the denizens of the garden. There is no treasure here.'
disagreements: Clue Book p.11-12 numbers the library 1-9 (1 History, 2 Rhetoric, 3 Philosophy, 4 Mathematics, 5 Storeroom, 6 Madman, 7 Master Scribe's Chamber, 8 Librarian's Chamber, 9 Garden); [P] uses 1 Garden, 2 Philosophy, 3 Mathematics, 4 History, 5 Rhetoric, 8, 11, 13, 14-16, 18. The numbers do not line up.
Game text says 'TAKING A GOOD DEAL OF DAMAGE'; [P] gives the amount as 1d4.
scenarios.notes: With fixed dice a runner can assert each roll. The digest does not say whether avoided encounters count toward the 7. [P] §5: ECL surprise opcodes apply the wrong modifiers; keep as in the original.

scenarios.title: Search Philosophy for Fyerdetha, Urgund and the marginal books
steps: Enter the Philosophy stacks (location 2). The game prints 'THESE ARE THE LIBRARY STACKS. OLD AND MOLDERING BOOKS ARE STORED ON SHELVES. A SIGN OVER THE ENTRANCE READS PHILOSOPHY.'
Search. The game prints 'AS YOU SEARCH THE ROOM YOU SCAN RANDOM BOOKS.'
Each search rolls 1 in 12 separately for each of three categories.
Category 1 hit: 'YOU FIND FYERDETHA'S DISCOURSES ON POWER. AMONG ALL THE DRY TEXT YOU FIND AN INTERESTING PASSAGE WHICH YOU COPY INTO YOUR JOURNAL AS ENTRY 7.'
Category 2 hit: 'YOU FIND URGUND'S DESCRIPTION OF DARKNESS. THIS IS AN ACCOUNT OF HIS IMPRISONMENT IN THE LOWER REALMS. THERE IS A PASSAGE OF INTEREST WHICH YOU COPY AS ENTRY 19 IN YOUR JOURNAL.'

Category 3 hit: 'YOU FIND A BOOK ENTITLED <title>', the titles always coming in this order: MEDITATIONS. / THE HARMONY OF THE ROCK. / STROM'S DISCUSSIONS OF POETICS. / CHRONICLES OF ARRAM. / DISCOURSE ON THE NATURE OF WRITING.
No hit: 'YOU FIND WORKS ON NATURAL PHILOSOPHY, THEORIES OF ART, AND THE SUPERNATURAL SCIENCES. IT IS VERY BORING.'
On a find the game asks 'DO YOU TAKE IT?' with YES / NO.
expect: Journal Entry 7 is recorded when Fyerdetha's Discourses on Power is found.
Journal Entry 19 is recorded when Urgund's Description of Darkness is found.
The five marginal books are found in the fixed order above.
Each book taken is carried by the party and arms the spectre exit trigger.
data: Journal Entry 7 (Adventurer's Journal p.17-18: scroll on pools of power, Fyerdetha)
Journal Entry 19 (Adventurer's Journal p.20: black tome naming Tyranthraxus the Flamed One among Bane's servants)
Marginal books in order: Meditations; The Harmony of the Rock; Strom's Discussions of Poetics; Chronicles of Arram; Discourse on the Nature of Writing
sources: Adventurer's Journal p.17-18 entry 7, p.20 entry 19
disagreements: Titles: Clue Book p.11 'Fyerdeth's Discourses on Power' and 'Urgund's Descriptions of Darkness'; game text and [P] 'FYERDETHA'S DISCOURSES ON POWER' and 'URGUND'S DESCRIPTION OF DARKNESS'.

Clue Book p.11-12 numbers the library 1-9 (1 History, 2 Rhetoric, 3 Philosophy, 4 Mathematics, 5 Storeroom, 6 Madman, 7 Master Scribe's Chamber, 8 Librarian's Chamber, 9 Garden); [P] uses 1 Garden, 2 Philosophy, 3 Mathematics, 4 History, 5 Rhetoric, 8, 11, 13, 14-16, 18. The numbers do not line up.
scenarios.notes: With fixed dice a runner can assert each of the three rolls per search. The digest does not say whether one search can yield more than one category at once, whether a found book can be found again, or what follows the fifth marginal book. The digest does not say whether books are inventory items; 'carrying at least one book' is the spectre condition, so some party state records them. The pairing of the 'DO YOU TAKE IT?' prompt (0x9962) with book finds is an inference; the digest does not mention it.

scenarios.title: Search Mathematics and find nothing
steps: Enter the Mathematics stacks (location 3). The game prints 'THESE ARE THE LIBRARY STACKS. OLD AND MOLDERING BOOKS ARE STORED ON SHELVES. A SIGN OVER THE ENTRANCE READS MATHEMATICS.'
Search. The game prints 'AS YOU SEARCH THE ROOM YOU SCAN RANDOM BOOKS.'
The game prints 'YOU FIND ESSAYS ON GEOMETRY, METAMAGICAL MATH, UNIVERSAL GEOMETRY, ETC., BUT NOTHING USEFUL.'
Search many more times.
expect: No book is ever found here.
sources: Clue Book p.11-12 location 4 'No special books here'

scenarios.title: Search History for the three histories
steps: Enter the History stacks (location 4). The game prints 'THESE ARE THE LIBRARY STACKS. OLD AND MOLDERING BOOKS ARE STORED ON SHELVES. A SIGN OVER THE ENTRANCE READS HISTORY.'
Search. The game prints 'AS YOU SEARCH THE ROOM YOU SCAN RANDOM BOOKS.'
Each search rolls 1 in 18 separately for each of three books.
'YOU FIND THE HISTORY OF THE NORTH. IT IS MOSTLY WRITTEN TO PLEASE A ROYAL LINE. HOWEVER, THERE IS AN INTERESTING PASSAGE WHICH YOU COPY INTO YOUR JOURNAL AS ENTRY 8.'
'YOU FIND LEX GEOGRAPHICA, AN ATLAS DRAWN BY TOMARUS. IT HAS A MAP OF PHLAN WHICH, THOUGH OLD, STILL COULD BE USEFUL. IT BECOMES ENTRY 37 IN YOUR JOURNAL.'
'YOU FIND THE GRAND HISTORIAN'S RECORDS OF THE ARTS OF WAR. IN IT YOU FIND A USEFUL PASSAGE WHICH YOU COPY INTO YOUR JOURNAL AS ENTRY 21.'
No hit: 'YOU FIND VARIOUS BOOKS WHICH ARE SO FILLED WITH MYTH THAT YOU DON'T FIND ANYTHING USEFUL.'
expect: Journal Entries 8, 37 and 21 are recorded as each book is found.
data: Journal Entry 8 (Adventurer's Journal p.18: account of the northern lands, The History of the North)
Journal Entry 37 (Adventurer's Journal p.25-26: atlas by Tomarus, maps of the Moonsea and Phlan)
Journal Entry 21 (Adventurer's Journal p.21: old book giving Tyranthraxus's history)
sources: Adventurer's Journal p.18 entry 8, p.21 entry 21, p.25-26 entry 37
disagreements: Clue Book p.11-12 numbers the library 1-9 (1 History, 2 Rhetoric, 3 Philosophy, 4 Mathematics, 5 Storeroom, 6 Madman, 7 Master Scribe's Chamber, 8 Librarian's Chamber, 9 Garden); [P] uses 1 Garden, 2 Philosophy, 3 Mathematics, 4 History, 5 Rhetoric, 8, 11, 13, 14-16, 18. The numbers do not line up.
scenarios.notes: Clue Book p.11: 'You may need to look in an area several times'. The Clue Book also says to stay in Search Mode; the digest's odds are per search and do not mention a search-mode bonus for books.

scenarios.title: Kill the basilisk in Rhetoric
steps: Equip mirrors on the party before entering.

Enter the Rhetoric stacks (location 5). The sign reads 'RHETORIC.' One of four basilisk texts prints, depending on surprise: 'AMID THE LITTER OF THE ROOM YOU SEE A DULL BROWN REPTILIAN MONSTER.' / 'YOU HEAR A HISS. AS YOU LOOK DOWN YOU SUDDENLY SEE A DULL BROWN REPTILIAN MONSTER.' / 'YOU SEE A DULL BROWN REPTILIAN MONSTER. IT DOESN'T SEEM AWARE OF YOU.' (menu COMBAT / WAIT / FLEE / APPROACH) / 'SUDDENLY, YOU SPOT A DULL BROWN REPTILIAN MONSTER WHICH IS JUST COMING AWAKE.'
Fight the BASILISK (#26).
Win and take the treasure.
expect: Each character gains 541 XP.
Treasure: Potion of Giant Strength, Potion of Healing, Cloak of Displacement, Clerical Scroll (Restoration, Restoration).
The basilisk half of the clear condition is met.
branches: Parley: does nothing ([P]); the encounter text is 'IT HISSES AT YOU.'
fights: BASILISK (#26), Morale 100, 541 XP; petrifying gaze, countered by mirrors
data: Potion of Giant Strength, Potion of Healing, Cloak of Displacement, Clerical Scroll (Restoration, Restoration)
sources: [P] §5 Adaptational: 'Non-random Cloaks of Displacement give no save bonus' (digest)
disagreements: Defence: [P] 'Equip mirrors first'; Clue Book p.11 'Be prepared with spells to raise your Saving Throws. Kill the basilisk before he gazes'. The Clue Book does not mention mirrors.

Clue Book p.11-12 numbers the library 1-9 (1 History, 2 Rhetoric, 3 Philosophy, 4 Mathematics, 5 Storeroom, 6 Madman, 7 Master Scribe's Chamber, 8 Librarian's Chamber, 9 Garden); [P] uses 1 Garden, 2 Philosophy, 3 Mathematics, 4 History, 5 Rhetoric, 8, 11, 13, 14-16, 18. The numbers do not line up.
scenarios.notes: Which of the four texts goes with which surprise result is not in the digest; read it from the script. The Cloak of Displacement found here is a non-random one, so per [P] §5 it gives no save bonus. Mirrors are sold at the New Phlan general store.

scenarios.title: Search Rhetoric and find nothing
steps: After the basilisk, search the Rhetoric stacks.
The game prints 'YOU FIND SPEECHES FROM FAMOUS MURDER TRIALS, PUBLIC DEBATES, ETC., BUT NOTHING OF INTEREST.'
expect: No book is found here.
scenarios.notes: The digest lists only the basilisk and its treasure at Rhetoric; the miss text is from the game text.

scenarios.title: Find the jar at location 8
steps: Walk to (8,11). The game prints 'YOU SEE A RUINED ROOM WITH ROTTED FURNITURE. HUMAN BONES LIE SCATTERED ABOUT A DESK.'
Search. The game prints 'YOU SEE A JAR UNDER THE FLOORBOARDS.' and 'DO YOU TAKE IT?' Choose YES.
expect: The party gains 3 Potions of Extra Healing.
Each character gains 200 XP.
sources: Clue Book p.11-12 locations 7-8 ('Search this room until you find the treasure')
disagreements: Clue Book p.11-12 numbers the library 1-9 (1 History, 2 Rhetoric, 3 Philosophy, 4 Mathematics, 5 Storeroom, 6 Madman, 7 Master Scribe's Chamber, 8 Librarian's Chamber, 9 Garden); [P] uses 1 Garden, 2 Philosophy, 3 Mathematics, 4 History, 5 Rhetoric, 8, 11, 13, 14-16, 18. The numbers do not line up.
scenarios.notes: The room description at 0xa5c5 directly precedes the jar line in the script; the pairing is by script order. Whether this is the Clue Book's Master Scribe's or Librarian's Chamber is not stated.

scenarios.title: Talk to the mad man at location 11
steps: Walk to (11,12). The game prints 'YOU FIND A FIGHTER WITH BATTERED ARMOR AND WILD EYES COWERING IN THE CORNER. 'YAI! MERCY! MERCY!' HE CRIES. AND THEN AS SUDDENLY, 'DIE! DIE YOU SLIME FROM THE PIT!'' with the menu COMBAT / WAIT / FLEE / PARLAY / IGNORE.
Choose PARLAY. The game prints 'THE MAN SCREAMS WHILE FROTHING AT THE MOUTH,' and one of four lines.
expect: One of: ''HE IS WRAPPED IN FIRE AND SO CRUEL!'' / ''THE BIG ONE, THE EVIL ONE IN THE CASTLE OF FLOWERS -- HE IS COMING! IT IS COMING!'' / ''DON'T GO THERE! DON'T GO ON THE HILL!'' / ''HE IS NOT HUMAN I TELL YOU! NOT AT ALL!''
branches: WAIT or IGNORE: 'WATCHING YOU WARILY, HE INCHES AWAY. WHEN HE IS OUT OF SWORD'S REACH HE SCRAMBLES TO HIS FEET AND FLEES THE ROOM.' (which choice prints this is not stated in the digest).
COMBAT: fight MAD MAN (#25); stats and XP not given in the digest.
fights: MAD MAN (#25); no composition details, morale or XP in the digest for fighting him
disagreements: Clue Book p.11-12 numbers the library 1-9 (1 History, 2 Rhetoric, 3 Philosophy, 4 Mathematics, 5 Storeroom, 6 Madman, 7 Master Scribe's Chamber, 8 Librarian's Chamber, 9 Garden); [P] uses 1 Garden, 2 Philosophy, 3 Mathematics, 4 History, 5 Rhetoric, 8, 11, 13, 14-16, 18. The numbers do not line up.
scenarios.notes: The digest does not say how the line is chosen (random or in order); a runner with fixed dice can pin it.

scenarios.title: Take the mad man into the party
steps: After the parley the game prints 'YOU SEE THE MAN IS QUITE MAD. DO YOU TAKE PITY AND INVITE HIM TO GO WITH YOU?' Choose YES.
The game prints 'HE LOOKS RELUCTANT AND SAYS, 'BUT HIS MINIONS ARE THERE. HE WILL COME TOO!' DO YOU INSIST HE COME?' Choose YES.
The game prints 'HE STANDS UP, MUTTERING TO HIMSELF, AND JOINS YOU.'
Walk him into New Phlan.
expect: MAD MAN (#25) is in the party as an NPC with Morale 0.
In New Phlan he randomly attacks citizens: 'THE MAD MAN SUDDENLY BEGINS TO SCREAM AND ATTACK EVERYONE WITHIN ARM'S REACH.' This is city-guard trigger (5).

A priest offers to take him: 'AN AGED PRIEST APPROACHES, POINTING AT THE MAD MAN, HE SPEAKS, 'THAT MAN URGENTLY NEEDS OUR CARE. DROP HIM FROM YOUR PARTY OR HE WILL BRING YOU TO GRIEF. WE WILL CARE FOR HIM.''
branches: Party already full: the join cannot happen (New Phlan's hiring text 'YOUR PARTY IS TOO LARGE TO JOIN AT THIS TIME' shows the engine limit; the library block has no such line, so the behaviour here is not documented).
sources: Clue Book p.11-12 location 6 'If he is with you when you return to town, he will cause trouble'
scenarios.notes: The digest says only that he 'can join with Morale 0 and causes trouble in town'. The odds of his outburst, where the priest appears, and what happens if he is dropped are not given; the priest's text is from the New Phlan game text. See acceptance.new-phlan for the city-guard consequences.

scenarios.title: Find the Manual of Bodily Health at location 13
steps: Walk to (13,13). The game prints 'THIS ROOM WAS ONCE A STUDY. IT IS NOW A SHATTERED RUIN.'
Search. The game prints 'BURIED AMID ALL THE TRASH YOU SEE A BOOK.' and 'DO YOU TAKE IT?' Choose YES.
expect: A Manual of Bodily Health is added to the party's items.
Each character gains 800 XP.
sources: [P] §5: 'The Manual of Bodily Health applies its HP adjustment wrongly'; Exploit 3 abnormal Constitution (digest)
disagreements: Effect: [P] '+1 Constitution after a month'; [GB] 'doesn't seem to do anything here'; [SP] 'worth 25,000 gold… we sold it' (digest §7 item 10).
scenarios.notes: The digest does not say whether the Manual counts as a 'book' for the spectre trigger; do not assume either way. The Clue Book says the search may need repeating ('Search this room until you find the treasure'); the digest gives no odds.

scenarios.title: Find the gold foil at locations 14, 15 and 16
steps: Enter the carrels. The game prints 'YOU ARE IN THE ILLUMINATORS CARRELS. ALL THEIR EQUIPMENT HAS DECAYED AND LIES ROTTING ON THE FLOOR.'
Search at 14, 15 and 16. The game prints 'AMID THE TRASH YOU FIND A BOX WHICH CONTAINS GOLD FOIL.' and 'DO YOU TAKE IT?'
expect: Across the three locations the party gains 3 Sheets of Gold.
The sheets are worthless (no sale value).
scenarios.notes: The digest gives no coordinates for 14/15/16 and does not say whether it is one sheet per location; '3 Sheets of Gold' over three locations is the literal reading.

scenarios.title: Spare the kobolds in the storeroom and get their map
steps: Walk to location 18 at (12,10). The game prints 'YOU HAVE ENTERED A STOREROOM FULL OF SUPPLIES TOO OLD TO BE USEFUL.' and 'LOOKING UP FROM A TABLE ARE FIVE KOBOLDS.' with the encounter text 'THEY PLEAD FOR MERCY.' / 'THEY STAND ARMS RAISED IN SURRENDER.'
The game prints 'ONE OF THE KOBOLDS SAYS, 'IF YOU SPARE OUR LIVES WE WILL TELL YOU ALL WE KNOW ABOUT THIS AREA!' WILL YOU SPARE THEM?' Choose YES.
The game prints 'THEY DESCRIBE THE SURROUNDING AREA TO YOU. YOU LISTEN CAREFULLY, QUESTION THEM AND FROM THIS, SKETCH A MAP INTO YOUR JOURNAL CALLING IT ENTRY 10.'
expect: Journal Entry 10 is recorded.
No combat occurs.
branches: Refuse or attack: fight 5 KOBOLD (#0), Morale 10; no map.
fights: 5 KOBOLD (#0), Morale 10 (they surrender); XP not given
data: Journal Entry 10 (Adventurer's Journal p.18: crude map marked 'X = BAD THINGS')
disagreements: Clue Book p.11: the kobolds give 'a map to part of the Cadorna Textile House'; the game text says they 'DESCRIBE THE SURROUNDING AREA'; the Journal's entry 10 is a crude map marked 'X = BAD THINGS' with no area named in NOTES.md.

Clue Book p.11-12 numbers the library 1-9 (1 History, 2 Rhetoric, 3 Philosophy, 4 Mathematics, 5 Storeroom, 6 Madman, 7 Master Scribe's Chamber, 8 Librarian's Chamber, 9 Garden); [P] uses 1 Garden, 2 Philosophy, 3 Mathematics, 4 History, 5 Rhetoric, 8, 11, 13, 14-16, 18. The numbers do not line up.
scenarios.notes: The digest says 'Accept -> map (JE 10)' without quoting the prompt; the prompt is from the game text.

scenarios.title: Visit the rooms with description only
steps: Visit the remaining rooms and read their texts: 'YOU SEE A CHAMBER FILLED WITH ROTTED FURNITURE AND BENCHES.'; 'YOU SEE AN EMPTY ROOM. THE ONLY FEATURE IS A SERIES OF FRESCOES ON THE WALLS OF LEARNED MEN AND THE HEAVENLY PATRONS OF ART AND LEARNING. YOU GET A FEELING OF PEACE.'; 'YOU ENTER A HALL WHICH IS FILLED WITH ROWS OF WRITING TABLES AND HIGH STOOLS. ROTTED MOUNDS OF PARCHMENT LITTER THE FLOOR.'; 'YOU ARE IN A SMALL ROOM HAVING LITTLE MORE THAN A BENCH AND A SMALL DESK.'
expect: Each text prints in its room; no fight, treasure or flag change follows.
scenarios.notes: None of these rooms is in the digest (its numbering skips 6, 7, 9, 10, 12, 17). Locations and coordinates must come from the script. That they are description-only is an inference from the absence of any guide entry; confirm in the script before asserting 'no flag change'.

scenarios.title: Leave with a book and fight the spectre
steps: Hold at least one library book.
Walk out through any exit for the first time.
The game prints 'A SPECTRE SUDDENLY APPEARS BEFORE YOU. 'THIEF! I DEFENDED THESE BOOKS IN LIFE AND I WILL DEFEND THEM IN DEATH!' IT ATTACKS YOU.'
Fight the SPECTRE (#17). The party cannot surprise it.
Win.
expect: Each character gains 338 XP.
The spectre half of the clear condition is met.
The spectre does not appear on later exits.
branches: Leave carrying no book: see leaving-without-books.
fights: SPECTRE (#17), Morale 100, 338 XP; cannot be surprised; level drain is implied by the type but not stated in the digest for this monster
sources: Adventurer's Journal p.35-36: a spectre can be turned only by a cleric of 5th level or higher
disagreements: Clue Book p.12: 'leave through one of the two doors. The spectre of the librarian will attack you as you leave if you have taken any books'; [P]: 'the first time you leave carrying at least one book', with three exits listed.
scenarios.notes: [P] lists 'magical weapons' under preparation; the digest does not say outright that the spectre needs them. The digest does not say what happens if the party flees the spectre, or whether the trigger re-arms.

scenarios.title: Leave without any book
steps: Enter, take no book, and leave.
Later enter again, take a book, and leave.
expect: No spectre appears on an exit made with no book.
The spectre appears on the first exit made with a book.
scenarios.notes: Consequence: the block cannot be cleared without taking at least one book, because the spectre is half of the clear condition, although 'the books do not matter' for the clear itself.

scenarios.title: Rest anywhere in the library
steps: Rest in several rooms, including the garden, for long periods.
expect: Per [P] the rest is never interrupted anywhere in the library.
sources: Clue Book p.11-12 'Where You Can Rest'
disagreements: [P]: 'Resting: always safe'. Clue Book p.11: 'The party can rest anywhere in the library except in the Garden.'
scenarios.notes: The two sources disagree about the garden. Read the garden's rest flag from the script and record which source the 1.3 data supports.

scenarios.title: Fleeing puts the party on one of four squares
steps: Flee from the basilisk, the mad man or the spectre.
Read the party position.
expect: The party is at one of (7,9), (5,5), (9,9), (9,11).

scenarios.title: Clear the library and collect commission #3
steps: Kill the basilisk and the spectre.
Go to the council clerk at New Phlan City Hall 29 (5,5).
The clerk pays commission #3.
expect: Reward: 200 platinum and 250 gold; each character gains 208 XP.
Commission #3 is resolved and drops off the clerk's list.
The quest tracker does not advance (#3 is not one of the ten tracker quests).
Any city-guard anger is cancelled.
data: Proclamation CXXVI (Adventurer's Journal p.13-15: books and tomes), posted at 2 tracker quests per [P]
sources: game text ECL3.DAX block 8 at 0xa927 (src/audio/voice-master-manifest.json) (offer: 'THE COUNCIL IS OFFERING A REWARD FOR BOOKS, MAPS, TOMES, ETC. ...')
game text ECL3.DAX block 8 at 0x9e4a (src/audio/voice-master-manifest.json) ('THERE IS A REWARD FOR CLEARING THE <area>')
disagreements: [P]: #3 is 'resolved by clearing Mendor's Library (basilisk + spectre)' and 'the books do not matter'. Clue Book p.12: 'The city council may continue to pester you for books, even after you have retrieved all five useful tomes'. The Clue Book ties the commission to books and says it can stay open; [P] ties it to the two kills.
scenarios.notes: 208 XP = (200 x 5 + 250) / 6. [P]: 'In some versions … never resolve this … [problem] with v1.0'; digest §5 lists 'Mendor's Library (v1.0): commission #3 may be unresolvable'. That is a v1.0 bug: do not require it in 1.3, where the commission must resolve. Which clerk line prints for this reward is not in the digest; the generic 'THERE IS A REWARD FOR CLEARING THE <area>' line is the likely one, to be confirmed in the script.

scenarios.title: Turn the books in to the clerk for bounties
steps: Carry the found books to the council clerk at City Hall 29 (5,5).
For each of the five named books the clerk prints a line and 'HERE IS YOUR REWARD.' and pays its bounty.
For the first marginal book the clerk pays 1 gold.
expect: Fyerdetha's Discourses on Power: 80 platinum, 66 XP each.
Urgund's Description of Darkness: 90 platinum, 75 XP each.
The Grand Historian's Records of the Arts of War: 120 platinum, 100 XP each.
The History of the North: 110 platinum, 91 XP each.
Lex Geographica: 100 platinum, 83 XP each.
The first of any other library book: 1 gold, 0 XP. Later marginal books pay nothing.
data: Clerk lines in the game text: 'WE FIND THESE DISCOURSES VALUABLE.' / 'THE COUNCIL WILL BE AMUSED BY THE DESCRIPTIONS.' / 'THESE MAPS SHOULD HELP US TO LOCATE SEVERAL LEGENDARY BUILDINGS.' / 'THESE HISTORIES CONTAIN MUCH USEFUL INFORMATION.' / 'THE RECORDS PROVIDE INSIGHTS INTO MUCH THAT WAS PUZZLING.' / 'THIS MATERIAL IS OF SMALL VALUE.'
disagreements: [P]: specific bounties (80/90/120/110/100 platinum; 1 gold for the first other book). [GB]: '9 books… each… around 500 total experience and 100 platinum' (digest §7 item 9).
scenarios.notes: The pairing of clerk lines to books is by wording (DISCOURSES = Fyerdetha, DESCRIPTIONS = Urgund, MAPS = Lex Geographica, HISTORIES = History of the North, RECORDS = Grand Historian's Records, SMALL VALUE = marginal book); the digest does not quote these lines, so confirm in the script. XP = platinum x 5 / 6 rounded down. The digest does not say whether the books are removed from the party on turn-in, or whether bounties count as a 'reward' that cancels city-guard anger.
